messages.subject: Announce: Workshops, St Andrews, Summer 2006
parts:
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Centre for Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling (CREEM)
University of St Andrews, St Andrews, Scotland

International Training Workshops in
Distance Sampling Methods for
Wildlife Population Assessment

http://www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/conferences.php
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

Registration for the following workshops is now open - see web site for
details. Note that we are also holding an introductory workshop in New
Zealand in June 2006 - again, see web site for details.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

Workshop 1: Introduction to Distance Sampling

This 3-day workshop will give participants a solid grounding in the basic
methods for design and analysis of distance sampling surveys for estimating
the density and/or abundance of wildlife populations. It is a blend of
theory and practice, and participants will learn how to use the industry-
standard program Distance. We will focus on "conventional" distance
sampling methods, as described in the standard reference book "Introduction
to Distance Sampling".

Workshop 2: Advanced Distance Sampling

This 2.5-day workshop will cover recent advances in distance sampling
research and software, as described in the book "Advanced Distance
Sampling". It is intended for those already familiar with conventional
distance sampling methods. We will teach advanced material such as
automated survey design, adaptive sampling, incorporating covariates into
the detection function and methods for where g(0)<1. Participants will learn
the more advanced features of Distance. Note that this workshop is
naturally complemented by the subsequent workshop on density surface
modelling.

Workshop 3: Primer on Density Surface Modelling from Distance Sampling Data

This new, 2.5-day workshop will focus on methods of predicting abundance or
density of biological data using the count method of Hedley and Buckland
(2004, Chapter 4 of "Advanced Distance Sampling"). Variation in animal
density/abundance is modelled as functions of covariates such as land cover
type, habitat, bathymetry, altitude or depth. General additive models (GAMs)
or general linear models (GLMs) will be fitted to estimated densities along
transects using a new analytical engine inside program Distance. This is an
advanced workshop for those already familiar with distance sampling.
Participants intending to model their own data will be required to have it
formatted according to precise specifications prior to arrival at St.
Andrews.

The workshops are aimed at wildlife managers, ecologists and statisticians.
All feature a mix of lectures and hands-on computer sessions. They are
taught by leading researchers from the Centre for Research into Ecological
and Environmental Modelling (CREEM) at St Andrews..
